manuscript_prose.section1_title: Deep Animal Origins, the Ctenophora–Porifera Root Debate & Basement-Membrane Assembly
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: Resolving the deepest divergences of Animalia—whether comb jellies (Ctenophora) or sponges (Porifera) form the sister lineage to all remaining metazoans alongside Placozoa, Cnidaria, and Bilateria—requires mitigating compositional heterogeneity and lineage-specific mitochondrial substitution-rate disparities across Neoproterozoic divergences.
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: In Version 4.0.0, all 64 stratified Holozoa and Basal Metazoa species ([A]–[G]) are analyzed across a 20-locus conserved nuclear coding and ribosomal RNA supermatrix under Standard Genetic Code 1, paired with Seo two-stage multilocus GENESITE bootstrap resampling, autocorrelated relaxed-clock dating, homogeneous Code-1 Hsp70, FoxJ1, SYT1, and COL4A1 selection models (PDB 1LI1), and 12 single-species conspecific marine coalescent skylines.
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Twenty-Locus Nuclear Partitioned ModelTest, RY3 De-Biasing & Tonian-to-Ediacaran Holozoa Chronogram
manuscript_prose.section3_title: 64-Species Quartet Multispecies Coalescent & Non-Bilaterian Phylum Concordance
manuscript_prose.section4_title: Purifying Constraint on Hsp70, FoxJ1 Ciliogenesis, Synaptotagmin-1 & Collagen IV NC1 (1LI1)
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Across verified Standard Genetic Code 1 metazoan coding orthologs, Goldman-Yang 61-state codon models quantify purifying constraint across thermal-stress chaperone Hsp70 (FAM-01), ciliogenesis regulator FoxJ1 (FAM-02), synaptic vesicle sensor SYT1 (FAM-03), and basement-membrane Type IV collagen COL4A1 (FAM-04) threaded onto PDB 1LI1 (1.90 Å).
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Conspecific Marine Skylines (Slow Anthozoan vs. Pelagic Scyphozoan/Ctenophore mtDNA) & Haplotype Networks
discussion_paragraphs: **Eliminating Mitochondrial Rate-Asymmetry Artifacts With a 20-Locus Nuclear Supermatrix.** Few deep phylogenetic problems are as sensitive to compartment choice and substitution modeling as the basal animal radiation [2–7, 16]. In mitochondrial supermatrices, shared slow circular-mtDNA evolution pulls Anthozoa toward Demospongiae while convergent Genetic Code 5 reassignments and elevated evolutionary rates pull Hexactinellida glass sponges and linear-mtDNA Medusozoa toward Bilateria, artificially splitting Cnidaria and Porifera [16]. Transitioning the phylogenetic backbone to 20 conserved nuclear coding and ribosomal loci (34,641 bp) under uniform Standard Genetic Code 1 with per-locus BIC rate multipliers and RY3 third-codon recoding reduces nucleotide compositional skew by 87.5% (RCFV = 0.0090) and resolves every non-bilaterian phylum in topological agreement with chromosome-scale BCnS linkage analyses [2, 11]: Ctenophora branches first as sister to Benthozoa, all four sponge classes fall outside Planulozoa, and monophyletic Cnidaria (Anthozoa + Medusozoa) forms the sister phylum to monophyletic Crown Bilateria (**Figures 1–3**).

**Tonian Stem Divergences Across Cryogenian Glaciations to Ediacaran Macrofossils.** Our autocorrelated relaxed-clock chronology places the Holozoa root (912.9 Ma) and Crown Metazoa (826.5 Ma) in the Tonian Period, followed by Benthozoa and Core Porifera–Planulozoa divergences (726.7–683.1 Ma) spanning the Tonian–Cryogenian transition and late Cryogenian–Ediacaran crown origins for Planulozoa (659.0 Ma), Core Porifera (646.4 Ma), Cnidaria (592.1 Ma), and Bilateria (550.7 Ma; **Table 2A**) [14]. These intervals align within credible bounds of published phylogenomic molecular timescales (e.g., dos Reis et al. [14]: Crown Metazoa ~750–833 Ma, Crown Bilateria ~550–585 Ma) and remain consistent with a protracted pre-Ediacaran interval of microscopic or soft-bodied stem metazoans prior to Avalon and White Sea macrofossil assemblages (~575–550 Ma) [8, 14, 15].

**Structural Conservation of Collagen IV Sulfilimine Crosslinks and Synaptic Exocytosis.** Codon selection models [19] and 3D structural threading onto PDB 1LI1 [12, 13] highlight conserved molecular foundations of animal tissue organization. Across Porifera (*Pseudocorticium*), Cnidaria (*Hydra*), and Bilateria, *COL4A1* preserves periodic *Gly-X-Y* repeats (**Supplemental Figure S1**) and a conserved NC1 fold (RMSD = 0.508 Å; TM-score = 0.9920; M0 dN/dS = 0.1045) framing the Met93–Hyl211 sulfilimine crosslink interface [12, 13]. Comparable purifying constraint on *FoxJ1* (98.0% purifying sites; ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0941) and *Synaptotagmin-1* (98.6% purifying sites; ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0661) supports deep conservation of the ancestral holozoan multiciliogenesis and Ca<sup>2+</sup>-triggered vesicle exocytosis machinery across basal metazoans [4, 5, 15].

**Conspecific Coalescent Skylines Quantify Anthozoan Mitochondrial Stasis.** Pairing maternal *COX1* skylines with conspecific nuclear *ITS1–5.8S* and *Hsp70* cohorts (**Figures 4A & 4B**) illustrates why mitochondrial barcoding lacks species-level resolution in reef-building anthozoans yet resolves intraspecific demography in medusozoans and ctenophores [4, 16]. *Acropora millepora* exhibits invariant *COX1* sequences (π = 0.0000) alongside polymorphic nuclear *Hsp70* (π = 0.0606), whereas pelagic *Aurelia* species and *Mnemiopsis leidyi* harbor informative mitochondrial diversity (*D* = −1.24 to −1.42).

**Limitations and Testable Hypotheses.** Three constraints bound these candidate inferences. First, 38 of the 64 species met the ≥70% nuclear supermatrix completeness threshold for concatenated ML and relaxed-clock dating—including *Bolinopsis microptera* (20/20 loci) in Ctenophora and seven sponges across all four Porifera classes—while the remaining 26 taxa with sparser public nuclear coverage (such as *Pleurobrachia*, *Beroe*, Cubozoa, and Staurozoa) are placed via 20-locus quartet coalescent reconciliation (**Figure 3**). Second, while edge-linked RY3 models and two-stage GENESITE resampling account for compositional skew and inter-locus variance (yielding cautious 65.2%–87.6% backbone bootstrap values rather than inflated site-only support), site-heterogeneous amino-acid mixture models (CAT-GTR / LG+C60) on expanded chromosomal proteomes remain important complementary tests of the Hexactinellida–Placozoa internode and root placement [2, 6, 7]. Third, Neoproterozoic node intervals remain contingent on soft fossil calibration priors pending unambiguous Tonian–Cryogenian body fossils [14].
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Reconstructing the earliest animal divergences across comb jellies, sponges, placozoans, cnidarians, and bilaterians requires overcoming lineage-specific mitochondrial rate asymmetry and third-codon saturation while tracking the evolution of basement membranes and neural signaling.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: evaluates deep animal divergences across 20 conserved nuclear loci, collagen IV selection, and conspecific marine demography across Basal Metazoa
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Sixty-four Holozoa and Metazoa taxa spanning unicellular outgroups [A] through Bilateria [G] are evaluated across 20 conserved nuclear loci (34,641 aligned bp) in Version 4.0.0.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: The evolutionary emergence of multicellular animals (Metazoa) from unicellular holozoan ancestors during the Neoproterozoic—and whether comb jellies (Ctenophora) or sponges (Porifera) represent the sister phylum to all other animals—remains a central question in evolutionary biology. Deep non-bilaterian phylogenetics on mitochondrial markers is confounded by lineage-specific evolutionary rate disparities between fast-evolving ctenophore, glass-sponge, medusozoan, and bilaterian mitogenomes versus slow-evolving demosponge, placozoan, and anthozoan mtDNA. Here, we assemble and analyze a 20-locus conserved nuclear supermatrix (18 single-copy nuclear housekeeping and informational coding genes plus nuclear 18S and 28S rRNA; 34,641 aligned base pairs; 20,178 parsimony-informative sites) across 64 holozoan species spanning Choanoflagellata, Filasterea, and Ichthyosporea outgroups, Ctenophora, all four classes of Porifera (Hexactinellida, Calcarea, Demospongiae, Homoscleromorpha), Placozoa, Cnidaria (Anthozoa, Medusozoa), and Bilateria. Edge-linked 20-locus BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced compositional heterogeneity by 87.5% (RCFV = 0.0090 vs. 0.0722 unrecoded and 0.0976 unphased; Δln L = +12,327.90 over unpartitioned RY3), recovering Ctenophora sister to Benthozoa, all Porifera outside Planulozoa, and monophyletic Cnidaria sister to monophyletic Bilateria across 38 completeness-gated (≥70%) taxa (mean multilocus GENESITE UFBoot2 = 79.4%) and 63 multi-locus species in quartet coalescent reconciliation (Q = 0.6575 across 2,660,245 quartets; 1,749,222 satisfied). Autocorrelated relaxed-clock dating places the Holozoa root in the Tonian at 912.9 Ma (95% HPD: 862.7–963.1 Ma), Crown Metazoa at 826.5 Ma (781.1–872.0 Ma), Benthozoa stem divergence at 726.7 Ma (686.7–766.6 Ma), Crown Planulozoa at 659.0 Ma (622.7–695.2 Ma), Crown Cnidaria at 592.1 Ma (559.6–624.7 Ma), and Crown Bilateria in the late Ediacaran at 550.7 Ma (520.4–581.0 Ma). Codon models across 36 deduplicated orthologs of Hsp70, FoxJ1, SYT1, and COL4A1 support purifying selection (M0 dN/dS = 0.1045–0.1169; zero BEB sites), while 3D threading onto the Type IV Collagen NC1 crystal structure (PDB 1LI1; TM-score = 0.9920) preserves the Met93–Hyl211 sulfilimine crosslink.
section1_paragraphs: The transition from unicellular and colonial holozoan protists (Choanoflagellata, Filasterea, and Ichthyosporea) to animals (Crown Metazoa) entailed major innovations in polarized epithelia, extracellular matrix scaffolding, motile multiciliogenesis, and chemical synaptic signaling [2, 8–12, 15]. At the center of early animal macroevolution lies the topological debate between two competing hypotheses for the sister group to all remaining animals: the classical "Porifera-sister" hypothesis, which interprets collar-flagellate choanocytes as homologous to choanoflagellates and favors a single origin of neurons and muscles in Eumetazoa [6–8, 15], versus the "Ctenophora-sister" hypothesis, supported by multiple nuclear phylogenomic matrices, ctenophore genome assemblies (*Bolinopsis microptera*, *Mnemiopsis leidyi*, *Pleurobrachia bachei*), and irreversible ancient chromosome-scale gene-linkage (BCnS synteny) fusions shared among sponges, cnidarians, and bilaterians to the exclusion of ctenophores [2–5, 11]. Resolving this root—together with the Neoproterozoic Tonian–Ediacaran timeline predating the Cambrian radiation [14]—constrains ancestral reconstructions of nervous systems, basement membranes, and epithelial polarity.

Compartment choice is decisive in non-bilaterian phylogenomics because mitochondrial genomes experience divergent architectural and genetic-code trajectories across early animal phyla [3, 4, 16]. Whereas demosponges, placozoans (*Trichoplax*), and anthozoan cnidarians retain circular mitochondrial chromosomes with among the lowest nucleotide substitution rates in eukaryotes—associated in octocorals with a mitochondrial *mtMutS* mismatch-repair gene—ctenophores possess compact ~10–11 kb mitogenomes with elevated evolutionary rates, medusozoan cnidarians (*Hydra*, *Rhopilema*, *Aurelia*) carry linear telomeric mitochondrial chromosomes, and hexactinellid glass sponges (*Oopsacas*, *Aphrocallistes*) independently evolved accelerated mitochondrial substitution rates alongside convergent Genetic Code 5 codon reassignments shared with bilaterians [4, 16]. Mitochondrial supermatrices consequently suffer cross-phylum long-branch attraction that pulls medusozoans and glass sponges toward Bilateria while excluding ctenophores. Replacing mitochondrial markers in the deep backbone with single-copy nuclear protein-coding and ribosomal RNA loci under uniform Standard Genetic Code 1 removes mitochondrial genetic-code convergence and compartment rate disparity while retaining mitogenomic population cohorts in downstream coalescent tests to quantify the rate paradox directly [2, 6, 7, 16].

Here, we analyze 351 curated holozoan and metazoan sequence records across 64 species (after automated sequence hygiene quarantined 1,803 partial, pseudogenic, or misannotated GenBank deposits) spanning 20 conserved nuclear partitions: *RPB1*, *RPB2*, *EF1A*, *EF2*, *VMA1*, *VMA2*, *RAD51*, *CCT*, *HSP70*, *HSP90*, *eIF5B*, *Sec61A*, *RPL8/uL2*, *RPL3/uL3*, *RPS3/uS3*, *FEN1*, *PCNA*, *ThrRS*, nuclear *18S* SSU rRNA, and nuclear *28S* LSU rRNA [1–3, 6, 7]. We combine edge-linked 20-locus BIC model selection, third-codon RY3 recoding, and Seo two-stage multilocus GENESITE bootstrap resampling with autocorrelated relaxed-clock dating [14], 63-species quartet multispecies coalescent reconciliation [17], and four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests, alongside 61-state Goldman–Yang codon selection [19] across *Hsp70*, *FoxJ1*, *Synaptotagmin-1* (*SYT1*) [4, 5], and Type IV collagen (*COL4A1*) threaded onto the 1.90 Å crystal structure of the collagen IV NC1 hexamer interface (PDB 1LI1) [12, 13], plus 12 single-species conspecific marine coalescent skylines and *COX1* haplotype networks [16, 18].
section2_paragraphs: Automated orthology curation and frame-locked Standard Genetic Code 1 translation across the 64 holozoan and metazoan species assembled a 20-locus nuclear supermatrix of 34,641 aligned base pairs containing 20,178 parsimony-informative RY3 sites and 22,535 distinct alignment patterns (**Supplemental Figure S3 & S4**) [1]. Per-locus BIC model selection with proportional rate multipliers (spanning *r* = 0.490× in *VMA2* and 0.502× in *Sec61A* to 1.603× in *ThrRS* and 2.426× in *CCT*) and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced relative composition frequency variability by 87.5%—from RCFV = 0.0722 under unrecoded four-state nucleotides and 0.0976 in unphased controls to RCFV = 0.0090—and improved marginal log-likelihood by Δln L = +12,327.90 nats (ln L = −557,662.32 vs. −569,990.22 unpartitioned RY3; ΔBIC = −22,648.9) across 38 high-completeness (≥70% bases and ≥8 loci) genomes spanning all seven taxonomic sectors ([A]–[G]; **Figures 1 & 2**; **Tables 3A, 3C & 3D**). Under Seo two-stage multilocus GENESITE resampling (B = 500), mean split support was 79.4% (range 55.0%–100.0%, compared with 97.0% under site-only unpartitioned resampling), reflecting genuine inter-locus variance across deep Neoproterozoic internodes.

Rooted on unicellular Holozoa outgroups ([A], *Salpingoeca rosetta* and *Capsaspora owczarzaki*), the 20-locus nuclear phylogeny and Thorne–Kishino autocorrelated relaxed-clock timetree recover clean phylum-level monophyly without mitochondrial long-branch artifacts (**Figures 1 & 2**; **Table 2A**) [2–5, 11, 14]. The Holozoa–Metazoa root (**Node I**) dates to the Tonian at 912.9 Ma (95% HPD: 862.7–963.1 Ma), followed by Crown Metazoa (**Node II**) at 826.5 Ma (95% HPD: 781.1–872.0 Ma) where Phylum Ctenophora ([B], *Bolinopsis microptera*; GENESITE UFBoot2 = 70.0%, quartet *q*<sub>1</sub> = 0.866, LPP = 0.9545) branches first as sister to Benthozoa. All seven completeness-gated Porifera species ([C], spanning Hexactinellida *Oopsacas minuta*, Calcarea *Sycon ciliatum*, Demospongiae *Amphimedon queenslandica*, *Halichondria panicea*, and *Dysidea avara*, and Homoscleromorpha *Oscarella lobularis* and *Corticium candelabrum*) plus Placozoa ([D], *Trichoplax* sp. H2) diverge across **Node III** (726.7 Ma (686.7–766.6 Ma); UFBoot2 = 87.6%) and **Node IV** (683.1 Ma (645.6–720.7 Ma); UFBoot2 = 78.8%), with Core Porifera diversifying at **Node V** (646.4 Ma (610.8–681.9 Ma)) and zero sponge lineages clustering inside Bilateria. Sister to core sponges, Crown Planulozoa / Eumetazoa (**Node VI**: 659.0 Ma (622.7–695.2 Ma)) splits into two reciprocally monophyletic clades: Phylum Cnidaria (**Node VII**: 592.1 Ma (559.6–624.7 Ma); UFBoot2 = 72.0%, uniting monophyletic Anthozoa [E, n = 12] and monophyletic Medusozoa [F, n = 5]) and Crown Bilateria / Nephrozoa (**Node VIII**: 550.7 Ma (520.4–581.0 Ma); UFBoot2 = 87.0%, *q*<sub>1</sub> = 0.615, LPP = 0.7996), which resolves Deuterostomia (Ambulacraria + Chordata), Spiralia (*Lingula* + *Crassostrea*), and Ecdysozoa (*Priapulus* sister to *Limulus* + Pancrustacea) [10, 14].
section3_paragraphs: To incorporate all 63 multi-locus holozoan and metazoan species—including additional ctenophores (*Mnemiopsis leidyi*, *Pleurobrachia bachei*, *Beroe ovata*), bathyal sponges (*Aphrocallistes vastus*, *Geodia barretti*, *Suberites domuncula*), placozoans (*Trichoplax adhaerens*, *Polyplacotoma mediterranea*), scyphozoans, cubozoans, and staurozoans represented by partial nuclear transcriptomes or rRNA panels—we reconciled individual maximum-likelihood gene trees across all 20 nuclear partitions under the quartet multispecies coalescent [1, 17]. Across 2,660,245 evaluated four-taxon quartets, the coalescent species tree satisfied 1,749,222 quartets, yielding normalized concordance Q = 0.6575 and mean local posterior probability LPP = 0.6965 (**Figure 3**; **Figure 6**; **Tables 2A & 3A**), while clustering all four ctenophore genera as a monophyletic basal metazoan lineage (*q*<sub>1</sub> = 0.866) and uniting all 12 bilaterians into a single monophyletic clade (*q*<sub>1</sub> = 0.615).

Four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests on the 20-locus nuclear alignment (**Figure 3C**; **Table 2B**) corroborate these deep relationships. Across the basal animal split, Ctenophora (*Bolinopsis*) exhibits balanced derived-allele sharing relative to Porifera (*Amphimedon*) and Cnidaria (*Nematostella*) rooted on Choanoflagellata (ABBA-1: BBAA = 551, ABBA = 369, BABA = 359, *D* = +0.0137, *Z* = 0.37), consistent with incomplete lineage sorting rather than cross-phylum introgression. Conversely, testing Placozoa (*Trichoplax*, P1) and Cnidaria (*Acropora*, P2) against Bilateria (*Branchiostoma*, P3) rooted on Calcarea (*Sycon*, O) reveals marked excess sharing of derived nuclear alleles between Cnidaria and Bilateria (ABBA-2: ABBA = 395 vs. BABA = 167, *D* = +0.4057, *Z* = 9.62), providing independent site-pattern support for Planulozoa (Cnidaria + Bilateria). Within Cnidaria (ABBA-3: *D* = −0.0259, *Z* = 0.60) and Nephrozoa (ABBA-4: *D* = 0.0000, *Z* = 0.00), discordant site patterns remain symmetric.
section4_paragraphs: Fitting 61-state Goldman–Yang codon substitution models [19] across 36 species-deduplicated metazoan coding orthologs aligned under Standard Genetic Code 1 indicates consistent purifying selection across all four multicellularity, ciliary, synaptic, and extracellular-matrix gene families (BEB Pr ≥ 0.95 = 0 sites across all four families; **Figure 5A–B**; **Table 4A**). Strongest site-level conservation governs the synaptic-vesicle exocytosis Ca<sup>2+</sup> sensor *Synaptotagmin-1* (*SYT1*, FAM-03; N = 8 species, 418 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1080, κ = 1.41; 98.6% of C2A/C2B codons at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0661) [4, 5] and the forkhead transcription factor *FoxJ1* regulating motile 9+2 ciliogenesis across choanoflagellates, sponge choanocytes, ctenophore comb rows, and eumetazoan epithelia (FAM-02; N = 12 species, 421 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1169, κ = 3.11; 98.0% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0941). Cytosolic chaperone *Hsp70* (FAM-01; N = 8 species, 572 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1106, κ = 1.70; 92.3% at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0872) and basement-membrane Type IV collagen α-chain *COL4A1* (FAM-04; N = 8 species spanning Porifera *Pseudocorticium*, Cnidaria *Hydra*, Ecdysozoa, and Vertebrata, 480 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1045, κ = 0.80; **Supplemental Figure S1**) likewise evolve under purifying constraint preserving periodic *Gly-X-Y* collagenous triplets and the C-terminal NC1 trimerization interface [12, 13].

Three-dimensional homology threading of metazoan *COL4A1* onto the 1.90 Å crystal structure of the Type IV Collagen NC1 domain (PDB 1LI1 Chain A; 228 Cα residues) [13] recovers conserved β-sheet subdomain geometry (Kabsch RMSD = 0.508 Å; TM-score = 0.9920; interface pocket volume = 107.6 Å<sup>3</sup>; **Figure 5D**). Sequence-to-structure mapping confirms retention of the intrachain disulfide core alongside the opposing Met93 and hydroxylysine/lysine-211 (Hyl211) residues that form the peroxidasin-catalyzed covalent sulfilimine crosslink (–S=N–), mechanically stabilizing epithelial basement membranes across Eumetazoa and homoscleromorph/demosponge lineages [12, 13].
section5_paragraphs: Twelve single-species conspecific Bayesian coalescent skylines (25,000 MCMC generations, 20% burn-in; ESS = 1,113.7–4,607.4; Gelman–Rubin R-hat = 1.0001–1.0031) quantify the mitochondrial substitution-rate paradox across non-bilaterian marine taxa (**Figures 4A & 4B**; **Table 4B**) [1, 16, 18]. Along Axis A (R1–R6, maternal *COX1*), pelagic scyphozoan moon jellies *Aurelia coerulea* (R1, N = 36, 498 bp, π = 0.0071, Tajima's *D* = −1.24) and *Aurelia aurita* (R2, N = 36, 507 bp, π = 0.0044, *D* = −0.26), circumboreal plumose anemone *Metridium senile* (R3, N = 36, 549 bp, π = 0.0028, *D* = −2.60), and pelagic ctenophore *Mnemiopsis leidyi* (R4, N = 20, 645 bp, π = 0.0087, *D* = −1.42) [4] retain informative intraspecific mitochondrial polymorphism tracking post-glacial and coastal range expansions, alongside Indo-Pacific reef corals *Pocillopora damicornis* (R5, N = 11, π = 0.0111, *D* = −1.93) and *Stylophora pistillata* (R6, N = 13, π = 0.0154, *D* = −0.59). Axis B (L1–L6) contrasts conspecific mitochondrial and nuclear loci directly [16]: in *Acropora millepora*, maternal mtDNA displays zero intraspecific polymorphism across 415 bp (L1, N = 12, π = 0.0000), whereas nuclear *Hsp70* CDS in *A. millepora* harbors substantial standing variation (L3, N = 10, 649 bp, π = 0.0606, *D* = +0.01), paralleled by conspecific nuclear *ITS1–5.8S* rDNA in *Stylophora pistillata* (L2, N = 13, 450 bp, π = 0.0600, *D* = +0.89; **Supplemental Figure S2**) and *Acropora hyacinthus* (L5, N = 20, 337 bp, π = 0.0497, *D* = −0.06), linear mtDNA in *Hydra vulgaris* (L4, N = 8, π = 0.0262, *D* = −1.45), and conspecific nuclear *Hsp70* in *Pocillopora damicornis* (L6, N = 36, 738 bp, π = 0.0040, *D* = −0.93).

Minimum-spanning and TCS *COX1* Folmer-overlap haplotype networks (**Figures 7A & 7B**) resolve 56 coastal scyphozoan and cnidarian reference sequences into 3 distinct clusters (29 unique haplotypes across 507 bp; *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9058) in Panel A and 53 anthozoan and hydrozoan sequences into 11 lineage clusters (19 unique haplotypes across 546 bp; *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.8425) in Panel B, visually contrasting shallow intraspecific coral *COX1* hubs against structured scyphozoan and hydrozoan demes.
manuscript_prose.section6_intro: Complete sequence-hygiene logs (including 1,803 quarantined deposits), Tonian–Ediacaran relaxed-clock intervals, clade recovery and ABBA–BABA site-pattern tests, 32-chain model selection rankings, 20-locus BIC rate multipliers, Goldman–Yang codon selection parameters, and 12 conspecific marine coalescent skyline summaries are compiled in **Tables 1–4C** below [1, 17–19].
